summary: Wythe County, VA steel tower built 1941 per NHLR; not in use; access by landowner permission only; registered 2014; marked standing by FFLA.

facts.status_note: Register says the tower is not in use; the most recent visit report on the Register is from August 30, 2010

access.note: Register says access is by permission of the landowner only; the 2010 visit report says there is no access road

events.note: Built field on the Register gives 1941; a 2010 visitor's recollection says before 1945
Visit report dated August 30, 2010 on the Register: needs paint, rot in the wood at the doorway, most glass broken, steel structure, stairs and rails seemed in very good condition

evidence.supports: location is Wythe County, Virginia, near Max Meadows
evidence.quote: Cove Mountain is an 83 feet tall steel tower located in Wythe County, VA

evidence.supports: near Max Meadows, Miller's Creek area
evidence.quote: It is near Max Meadows, in the Miller's Creek area.

evidence.supports: tower built in 1941 per the Register's Built field
a 2010 visitor recalls the tower was built before 1945 with materials carried up by convicts, per a local resident; unverified
evidence.quote: Built sometime before 1945, materials carried to the top of the mountain by convicts, according to an 82 year old local

evidence.supports: tower has not been used for many decades
evidence.quote: Tower has not been used in many decades.

evidence.supports: tower is not in use and access is by permission of the landowner only
evidence.quote: Tower is not in use. Access to the tower is by permission of the landowner only.

evidence.supports: no access road to the tower
steel structure, stairs and rails seemed to be in very good condition at the 2010 visit (the visitor's word is 'seem')
evidence.quote: Steel structure, stairs, rails all seem to be in very good condition.

evidence.supports: some rotting of the wood at the doorway at the 2010 visit; the visitor was wary of the wood cab floor but did not report it rotten
evidence.quote: there is some rotting of the wood at the doorway

evidence.supports: most glass broken at the 2010 visit
the Forest Fire Lookout Association's Virginia list marks the tower as standing
the 2010 visitor estimated the tower at least 60 feet tall without measuring it
evidence.quote: Tower is at least 60' tall, but I did not determine the exact height.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Register gives 83 feet; the 2010 visit report says the tower is at least 60 feet tall but was not measured. The figures do not conflict. We use the Register's 83 feet.
The Register's Built field gives 1941; the 2010 visit report recalls a build date before 1945 from a local resident. These are compatible. We use 1941 and record the recollection as unverified.

notes_for_editor: Built year and registration date and design come from the Register's own fields. Access and condition rest on one 2010 visit report, which is sixteen years old. The brief's access 'unknown' is replaced with permission. The 1941 built date and the visitor's pre-1945 recollection are compatible but only the Register field is used as the date. Visitor report names are left out of the story. Second search returned only general material; no independent history found. Elevation in the brief (1017.4 m) matches the Register's 1,017 m. The story does not include coordinates.
